title: Recording: C Moon by Wings | 1972
content:
Studio One, Morgan Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Mike Bobak

Wings began recording ‘C Moon’ on 2 September 1972.

The song emerged from a studio improvisation the previous day.

This session featured Led Zeppelin’s John Bonham on drums. Bonham knew Denny Laine, and was invited to Morgan Studios at Paul McCartney’s request. At the time Wings’ drummer Denny Seiwell was travelling to England from New York.

Bonham jammed with the rest of Wings, before guitarist Henry McCullough took to the drum stool for the recording of ‘C Moon’. Take six became the master, after which the band and Bonham continued jamming.

John Bonham of Zeppelin was down the night we did ‘C Moon’ at Morgan Studios, which was a crazy nigh. He was down there, he brought some things with him, it was a good laugh – we had a crazy evening.
Paul McCartney
Melody Maker, 2 December 1972
